title: Repeating Patterns: What Comes Next?
seo_title: Foundation Repeating Patterns Worksheets: AB, AAB and ABC Patterns (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise, copy and continue repeating patterns represented in different ways.
meta_desc: Free Foundation (Prep, Kindergarten) maths worksheets on repeating patterns, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9MFA01): what comes next, AB, AAB and ABC patterns, the part that repeats, missing pieces, sounds and actions. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: A repeating pattern has a part that comes again and again.
key_sub: Find the part that repeats, then say it over and over to keep going.
body_html:
What is a repeating pattern?

A repeating pattern has a part that comes again and again. Find that part, then say it over and over to keep going.

Longer parts

Some patterns repeat 3 things: two the same then one different (AAB), or three different things (ABC).

Different ways

Patterns can be colours, shapes, sounds or actions: clap, stamp, clap, stamp is an AB pattern too.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Repeating the last thing againSay the pattern from the start
Right shape, wrong colourCheck both the shape and the colour
Naming only part of the repeating partFind where the pattern starts again

faq.q: What patterns do Foundation students learn?
faq.a: Repeating patterns: they recognise, copy and continue patterns made with colours, shapes, objects, sounds and actions (AC9MFA01).

faq.q: What do AB, AAB and ABC mean?
faq.a: They describe the part that repeats. AB is two things taking turns (red, blue). AAB is two the same then one different. ABC is three different things.

faq.q: Why are patterns important in maths?
faq.a: Spotting what repeats is the start of algebra. It also helps with counting by 2s, 5s and 10s and with days of the week.

faq.q: How can I make patterns at home?
faq.a: Thread beads, line up toys, or clap and stamp a rhythm. Ask your child to say what comes next and which part repeats.

items.q: Which pattern is made the same way as red, blue, red, blue, red, blue?
c: dog, dog, cat, dog, dog, cat
red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue
circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle
green, yellow, green, yellow, green, yellow
items.e: Both are one, then another, again and again patterns: the parts repeat in the same way. green, yellow, green, yellow, green, yellow.
